$comment: Pinned examples with HUMAN labels. Run `judge.py --calibrate` before trusting a
judge model, and again after any rubric edit or judge-model change.
These four cases are deliberately unambiguous. A judge that cannot reproduce an
obvious label within 1 point is not going to be right on the ambiguous ones, and
you would never find out — that is what makes an uncalibrated judge dangerous
Add your own cases from real disagreements you resolve. That is how a rubric
stops being a document and starts being an instrument.
